questions.stem: A body in surroundings at $20^\circ\text{C}$ cools from $84^\circ\text{C}$ to $52^\circ\text{C}$ in $6$ min. Assuming Newton’s law of cooling holds, how long will it take to cool further to $28^\circ\text{C}$?
questions.solution:
By Newton’s law of cooling, the excess temperature halves every $6$ min: $
\frac{52-20}{84-20}=\frac12$.
From $52^\circ\text{C}$ to $28^\circ\text{C}$, the excess temperature falls from $32^\circ\text{C}$ to $8^\circ\text{C}$, i.e. two halvings; hence $t=2(6)=12$ min.

questions.stem: A projectile is launched from level ground at $20$ m s$^{-1}$ at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Taking $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$, what is its horizontal range?
questions.solution:
For a projectile returning to the same level, $R=\dfrac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g}$.
$$R=\dfrac{20^2\sin 60^\circ}{10}=20\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$$

questions.stem: A radioactive sample has a half-life of $6$ h. What fraction of its original nuclei remains after $24$ h?
questions.solution:
The number of half-lives elapsed is $n=\dfrac{24}{6}=4$. Hence,
$$\dfrac{N}{N_0}=\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^4=\dfrac{1}{16}.$$

questions.stem: A $0.20$ m amplitude spring–mass oscillator has spring constant $200$ N m$^{-1}$. What is its kinetic energy when its displacement from the mean position is $0.12$ m?
questions.solution:
For a spring–mass oscillator, $K=\frac12 k(A^2-x^2)$. Substituting the given values,
$$K=\frac12(200)(0.20^2-0.12^2)=2.56\ \text{J}$$

questions.stem: A cell of emf $12$ V and internal resistance $1\ \Omega$ is connected to a $5\ \Omega$ resistor as shown in the figure. What is the power dissipated in the cell's internal resistance?
questions.solution:
The total resistance is $R=5+1=6\ \Omega$, so the current is $I=\dfrac{12}{6}=2\ \text{A}$. The power dissipated in the internal resistance is
$$P=I^2r=(2)^2(1)=4\ \text{W}.$$

questions.stem: Two fixed charges, $+4\ \mu\text{C}$ and $+1\ \mu\text{C}$, are $30$ cm apart. How far from the $+4\ \mu\text{C}$ charge should a nonzero third charge be placed between them so that the net force on it is zero?
questions.solution:
Between the charges, the electric fields oppose. For zero net force, their magnitudes must be equal:
$$\frac{k(4)}{x^2}=\frac{k(1)}{(30-x)^2}\quad\Rightarrow\quad \frac{2}{x}=\frac{1}{30-x}$$
Solving gives $x=20\text{ cm}$ from the $+4\,\mu\text{C}$ charge.

questions.stem: A person on a rotating stool pulls in their arms. The combined moment of inertia of the person and stool changes from $4.0$ kg m$^2$ to $2.5$ kg m$^2$. If the initial angular speed is $3.0$ rad s$^{-1}$ and external torque is negligible, what is the final angular speed?
questions.solution:
With negligible external torque, angular momentum is conserved:
$$I_i\omega_i=I_f\omega_f$$
Thus, $\omega_f=\dfrac{4.0}{2.5}(3.0)=4.8\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$.

questions.stem: A long air-core solenoid has $1000$ turns per metre and carries a current of $4$ A. Find the magnetic field at its centre. Take $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \text{T m A}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
For a long air-core solenoid, $B=\mu_0 nI$.
$$B=(4\pi\times10^{-7})(1000)(4)=1.6\pi\times10^{-3}\ \text{T}$$

questions.stem: A series LCR circuit has resistance $6\ \Omega$, inductive reactance $13\ \Omega$ and capacitive reactance $5\ \Omega$. What is its power factor?
questions.solution:
Net reactance is $X_L-X_C=13-5=8\ \Omega$, so the impedance is
$$Z=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\ \Omega.$$
Hence, the power factor is $\cos\phi=R/Z=6/10=0.6$.

questions.stem: The density of a sphere is calculated from its measured mass $m$ and radius $r$ using $\rho=\dfrac{3m}{4\pi r^3}$. If the percentage errors in $m$ and $r$ are $2\%$ and $1\%$, respectively, what is the maximum percentage error in $\rho$?
questions.solution:
For $\rho\propto mr^{-3}$, the maximum fractional error is $\dfrac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}=\dfrac{\Delta m}{m}+3\dfrac{\Delta r}{r}$.
Thus, maximum percentage error $=2\%+3(1\%)=5\%$.

questions.stem: A gas undergoes the cycle shown in the P–V diagram. Find the net work done by the gas per cycle and state whether the cycle is clockwise or anticlockwise.
questions.solution: The net work done by the gas is the signed area enclosed by the cycle. For the triangular loop, $|W|=\frac12\Delta P\Delta V=\frac12(3\times10^5)(2\times10^{-3})=300\,\text{J}$. The anticlockwise cycle gives $W_{\text{by gas}}=-300\,\text{J}$.

questions.stem: A concave mirror forms a real image with magnification $-\dfrac{1}{2}$ when an object is placed $24\ \text{cm}$ in front of it. What is the mirror’s focal length?
questions.solution:
Using $m=-v/u$, with $u=-24\ \text{cm}$, we get $v=-12\ \text{cm}$.
$$\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}=-\frac{1}{12}-\frac{1}{24}=-\frac{1}{8}\ \text{cm}^{-1}$$
Hence the focal length has magnitude $8\ \text{cm}$.

questions.stem: A stone is dropped from rest from a height of $45$ m above the ground. Ignoring air resistance, what is its speed just before impact? Take $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$.
A soap bubble of radius $5.0$ mm is formed in air. If the surface tension of the soap solution is $0.025$ N m$^{-1}$, what is the excess pressure inside the bubble?

questions.stem: In a Young’s double-slit experiment, the arrangement is as shown in the figure. For light of wavelength $600$ nm, find the fringe width when the slit separation is $0.30$ mm and the screen is $1.5$ m away.
questions.solution:
The fringe width in Young’s double-slit experiment is $\beta=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$.
$$\beta=\dfrac{(600\times10^{-9})(1.5)}{0.30\times10^{-3}}=3.0\times10^{-3}\,\text{m}=3\,\text{mm}$$

questions.stem: A $12\ \text{V}$ battery is connected to the capacitor network as shown in the figure. What are its equivalent capacitance and the charge on the $6\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor?
questions.solution:
The $3\,\mu\text{F}$ and $6\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitors are in parallel, and their combination is in series with the other $3\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor.
$$C_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{3\times(3+6)}{3+(3+6)}=2.25\,\mu\text{F}$$
The parallel combination has voltage $V=27/9=3\,\text{V}$, so $Q_6=6\times3=18\,\mu\text{C}$.

questions.stem: For a uniform solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$, let $V_c,V_m,V_s$ be the gravitational potentials at $r=0,R/2,R$, respectively, and let $g_c,g_m,g_s$ be the corresponding field magnitudes. Which combined ordering is correct?
questions.solution:
Inside a uniform solid sphere, $V(r)=-\dfrac{GM}{2R^3}(3R^2-r^2)$ and $g(r)=\dfrac{GMr}{R^3}$.
$$V_c=-\frac{3GM}{2R},\quad V_m=-\frac{11GM}{8R},\quad V_s=-\frac{GM}{R};\qquad g_c=0,\quad g_m=\frac{GM}{2R^2},\quad g_s=\frac{GM}{R^2}$$
Hence, $V_c<V_m<V_s<0$ and $g_c<g_m<g_s$.

questions.stem: The magnetic flux through each turn of a $20$-turn coil decreases uniformly from $8$ mWb to $2$ mWb in $0.03$ s. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf in the coil?
questions.solution:
By Faraday’s law, the magnitude of the average induced emf is
$$|\mathcal{E}_{\rm avg}|=N\frac{|\Delta\Phi|}{\Delta t}=20\frac{(8-2)\times10^{-3}}{0.03}=4\,\text{V}.$$

questions.stem: A proton and an $\alpha$ particle are accelerated from rest through the same potential difference. Taking the $\alpha$ particle’s mass as $4m_p$ and its charge as $2e$, what is the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths, $\lambda_p: \lambda_\alpha$?
questions.solution:
For a particle accelerated from rest through potential $V$, $p=\sqrt{2mqV}$ and $\lambda=h/p$. Thus,
$$\frac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{m_\alpha q_\alpha}{m_pq_p}}=\sqrt{\frac{(4m_p)(2e)}{m_pe}}=2\sqrt{2}$$
Hence, $\lambda_p:\lambda_\alpha=2\sqrt{2}:1$.

questions.stem: An astronomical telescope is in normal adjustment, as shown in the figure. The focal lengths of its objective and eyepiece are marked. What is its magnifying power?
questions.solution:
For a telescope in normal adjustment, the magnifying power is $M=\dfrac{f_o}{f_e}$.
$$M=\dfrac{80}{4}=20$$

questions.stem: A person stands on a scale in a lift accelerating downward at $2.5\ \text{m s}^{-2}$. Taking $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, what is the scale reading as a fraction of the person’s true weight $mg$?
questions.solution:
For downward acceleration $a$, the scale reading is the normal force $N=m(g-a)$.
$$N=m(10-2.5)=0.75mg=\dfrac34mg$$

questions.stem: A wheel rolls without slipping to the right with its centre moving at $4$ m s$^{-1}$. What is the speed of a point at the rightmost edge of the rim?
questions.solution:
For rolling without slipping, the rotational speed of the rim is $v_{\text{cm}}=4\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. At the rightmost point, this velocity is perpendicular to the centre’s velocity, so
$$v=\sqrt{4^2+4^2}=4\sqrt{2}\ \text{m s}^{-1}.$$

questions.stem: In the circuit shown, an ideal Zener diode maintains the load voltage at its breakdown voltage. Find the current through the Zener diode when the input is $12$ V.
questions.solution:
The Zener clamps the load voltage at $6\ \text{V}$. The series current is $I_s=\dfrac{12-6}{200}=30\ \text{mA}$, while the load current is $I_L=\dfrac{6}{300}=20\ \text{mA}$.
$$I_Z=I_s-I_L=30-20=10\ \text{mA}$$

questions.stem: Three coplanar concurrent forces are in equilibrium. Two forces of $6$ N and $8$ N act at angles of $0^\circ$ and $90^\circ$, respectively, to the positive $x$-axis. What is the magnitude of the third force?
questions.solution:
For equilibrium, the third force must be equal and opposite to the resultant of the first two forces.
$$F_3=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\,\text{N}$$

questions.stem: A wire of resistance $R$ is stretched uniformly until its length increases by $20\%$. Assuming its volume and resistivity remain constant, its new resistance is:
questions.solution:
With volume constant, $AL$ is constant, so $R=\rho L/A\propto L^2$.
$$\frac{R'}{R}=(1.20)^2=1.44$$
Thus, the new resistance is $1.44R$.

questions.stem: A source emitting a tone of frequency $500\ \text{Hz}$ moves towards and, after passing, away from a stationary observer at the same speed, $30\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. If the speed of sound is $330\ \text{m s}^{-1}$, find the ratio of the observed frequencies before and after passing.
questions.solution:
For a moving source, $f_{\text{toward}}=f\dfrac{v}{v-u}$ and $f_{\text{away}}=f\dfrac{v}{v+u}$. Hence,
$$\dfrac{f_{\text{toward}}}{f_{\text{away}}}=\dfrac{v+u}{v-u}=\dfrac{330+30}{330-30}=\dfrac{6}{5}$$

questions.stem: A series LCR circuit has $R=10\ \text{\Omega}$, $L=0.5\ \text{H}$ and $C=50\ \mu\text{F}$. Its quality factor at resonance is:
questions.solution:
For a series LCR circuit, $Q=\frac{\omega_0L}{R}$, where $\omega_0=\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$.
$$\omega_0=\frac{1}{\sqrt{(0.5)(50\times10^{-6})}}=200\ \text{rad s}^{-1},\qquad Q=\frac{(200)(0.5)}{10}=10.$$

questions.stem: In a hydrogen atom, an electron makes a transition from the $n=4$ level to the $n=2$ level. The energy of the emitted photon is:
questions.solution:
For a transition from $n_i=4$ to $n_f=2$, the emitted photon energy is
$$E_\gamma=13.6\left(\frac{1}{n_f^2}-\frac{1}{n_i^2}\right)=13.6\left(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{16}\right)=2.55\ \text{eV}.$$

questions.stem: For the logic circuit shown in the figure, the output $Y$ is:
questions.solution:
The first two gates give $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{CD}$. Applying De Morgan’s law at the final NAND gate,
$$Y=\overline{\overline{AB}\,\overline{CD}}=AB+CD.$$

questions.stem: Light of wavelengths $310\ \text{nm}$ and $620\ \text{nm}$ falls separately on the same metal, whose work function is $1.0\ \text{eV}$. Given $hc=1240\ \text{eV nm}$, find the ratio of the maximum kinetic energies for $310\ \text{nm}$ and $620\ \text{nm}$ light.
questions.solution:
Using the photoelectric equation, $K_{\text{max}}=hc/\lambda-\phi$:
$$K_{310}=1240/310-1=3\ \text{eV},\qquad K_{620}=1240/620-1=1\ \text{eV}$$
Hence, $K_{310}/K_{620}=3/1=3$.

questions.stem: A $2\ \text{kg}$ block moving at $8\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ collides with a stationary $6\ \text{kg}$ block on a smooth surface, and they stick together. How much kinetic energy is lost in the collision?
questions.solution:
By conservation of momentum, the common speed after collision is
$$v=\frac{(2)(8)}{2+6}=2\ \text{m s}^{-1}.$$
The kinetic energy lost is $K_i-K_f=\frac12(2)(8^2)-\frac12(8)(2^2)=64-16=48\ \text{J}$.

questions.stem: A square loop of side $0.40\ \text{m}$ carries a current of $5.0\ \text{A}$. Find the magnitude of the magnetic field at its centre. Take $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \text{T m A}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
The field due to a finite straight wire is $B_1=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}(\sin\theta_1+\sin\theta_2)$. Here $r=a/2$ and $\theta_1=\theta_2=45^\circ$, so
$$B=4B_1=\frac{2\sqrt{2}\mu_0 I}{\pi a}=1.0\times10^{-5}\sqrt{2}\ \text{T}.$$

questions.stem: A cyclist covers the first half of a journey at $12$ m s$^{-1}$ and the second half at $8$ m s$^{-1}$. What is the average speed for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
For equal distances, average speed is the harmonic mean of the two speeds:
$$v_{\text{avg}}=\frac{2v_1v_2}{v_1+v_2}=\frac{2(12)(8)}{12+8}=9.6\text{ m s}^{-1}.$$

questions.stem: A plane electromagnetic wave of intensity $1.2\times10^3\ \text{W m}^{-2}$ is incident normally on a surface of area $0.50\ \text{m}^2$. Find the difference between the forces when the surface is perfectly reflecting and perfectly absorbing. Take $c=3.0\times10^8\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
For absorption, $F_{\text{abs}}=IA/c$; for perfect reflection, $F_{\text{refl}}=2IA/c$. Thus,
$$F_{\text{refl}}-F_{\text{abs}}=\frac{IA}{c}=\frac{(1.2\times10^3)(0.50)}{3.0\times10^8}=2.0\times10^{-6}\ \text{N}$$

questions.stem: In a double-slit experiment with equal-intensity slits, the path difference at a point is $\dfrac{\lambda}{3}$. What is the intensity there as a fraction of the maximum intensity?
questions.solution:
The phase difference is $\phi=\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\Delta x=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$. For equal-intensity slits,
$$\dfrac{I}{I_{\max}}=\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)=\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\dfrac{1}{4}.$$

questions.stem: A travelling wave is described by $y=0.02\cos(8\pi t+4\pi x)$ m, where $x$ is in metres and $t$ is in seconds. What are its amplitude, wavelength, frequency, speed and direction of propagation, respectively?
questions.solution:
$A=0.02\,\text{m}$, $\omega=8\pi\,\text{rad s}^{-1}$ and $k=4\pi\,\text{rad m}^{-1}$. Thus $f=\omega/(2\pi)=4\,\text{Hz}$ and $\lambda=2\pi/k=0.5\,\text{m}$.
$$v=\frac{\omega}{k}=2\,\text{m s}^{-1}$$The phase $kx+\omega t$ travels in the $-x$ direction.

questions.stem: At the same temperature, compare the rms speeds of molecules of hydrogen, H$_2$, and oxygen, O$_2$. What is the ratio $v_{\text{rms}}(\text{H}_2)/v_{\text{rms}}(\text{O}_2)$? Take their molar masses as $2$ g mol$^{-1}$ and $32$ g mol$^{-1}$, respectively.
questions.solution:
At fixed temperature, $v_{\text{rms}}\propto 1/\sqrt{M}$.
$$\frac{v_{\text{rms}}(\text{H}_2)}{v_{\text{rms}}(\text{O}_2)}=\sqrt{\frac{32}{2}}=4$$

questions.stem: A temperature of $50^\circ$F is equivalent to what temperature on the Celsius scale?
questions.solution:
Use the conversion formula $T_C=\frac{5}{9}(T_F-32)$. Substituting $T_F=50$ gives
$$T_C=\frac{5}{9}(50-32)=10^\circ\text{C}.$$

questions.stem: A wire of length $2$ m and cross-sectional area $4\times10^{-6}$ m$^2$ is stretched by a load of $400$ N. If its Young's modulus is $2\times10^{11}$ Pa, what is its elongation?
questions.solution:
Young’s modulus is $Y=\dfrac{FL}{A\Delta L}$, so
$$\Delta L=\dfrac{FL}{AY}=\dfrac{400\times2}{(4\times10^{-6})(2\times10^{11})}=1\times10^{-3}\text{ m}.$$

questions.stem: On heating 1-bromo-2-methylpropane with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$, then treating the alkene with $\text{HBr}$ in the absence of peroxide, the major product is:
questions.solution:
Alcoholic KOH causes β-elimination to form 2-methylpropene:
$$\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}} \text{CH}_2=\text{C(CH}_3)_2$$
In the absence of peroxide, HBr adds by Markovnikov’s rule, placing Br on the more substituted carbon to give $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}$, 2-bromo-2-methylpropane.

questions.stem: A solution is prepared by dissolving $9.2$ g of glycerol (molar mass $92\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$) in $100$ g of water. Find its freezing point if $K_f=1.86\ ^\circ\text{C kg mol}^{-1}$ and pure water freezes at $0\ ^\circ\text{C}$.
questions.solution:
Moles of glycerol $=\frac{9.2}{92}=0.10$ mol; molality $=\frac{0.10}{0.100}=1.0\ \text{mol kg}^{-1}$.
$$\Delta T_f=K_fm=1.86\times1.0=1.86^\circ\text{C}$$
Hence, $T_f=0-1.86=-1.86^\circ\text{C}$.

questions.stem: A first-order reaction starts with $80$ mg of reactant; $10$ mg remains after $6$ h. What is its half-life?
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, $N/N_0=(1/2)^n$. Here, $10/80=1/8=(1/2)^3$, so 6 h corresponds to 3 half-lives.
$$t_{1/2}=\frac{6}{3}=2\text{ h}$$

questions.stem: Which of the following vitamins is fat-soluble?
questions.solution: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, while B vitamins and vitamin C are water-soluble. Hence, vitamin D is fat-soluble.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes chlorine-radical-catalysed ozone depletion?

options.text: CFCs release chlorine radicals mainly by reaction with water vapour in the troposphere.
A chlorine radical is permanently consumed after reacting with an ozone molecule.
A chlorine radical is regenerated, and the net reaction is $\text{O}_3+\text{O}\rightarrow2\text{O}_2$.
CFCs initiate ozone depletion by photolysis with visible light.

questions.solution:
Chlorine radicals catalyse ozone depletion through the steps
$$\text{Cl}\boldsymbol{\cdot}+\text{O}_3\rightarrow\text{ClO}\boldsymbol{\cdot}+\text{O}_2,\qquad \text{ClO}\boldsymbol{\cdot}+\text{O}\rightarrow\text{Cl}\boldsymbol{\cdot}+\text{O}_2.$$
The chlorine radical is regenerated; the net reaction is $\text{O}_3+\text{O}\rightarrow2\text{O}_2$.

questions.stem: On adding Lucas reagent to primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols, which one gives immediate cloudiness, and why?

options.text: Primary alcohol; it forms the most stable carbocation
Secondary alcohol; it forms the most stable carbocation
Tertiary alcohol; it reacts by an $S_{N2}$ mechanism
Tertiary alcohol; it forms the most stable carbocation

questions.solution:
Lucas reaction proceeds mainly by the $S_N1$ mechanism, whose rate depends on carbocation stability:
$$3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$$
Tertiary alcohol forms the most stable carbocation and reacts fastest, giving immediate cloudiness.

questions.stem: What are the geometry and hybridisation of the central atom in $\text{XeF}_4$?
questions.solution:
Xe has 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs, so there are 6 electron domains around the central atom.
$$\text{Hybridisation}=sp^3d^2$$
The two lone pairs occupy opposite positions in an octahedral arrangement, leaving a square-planar molecular geometry.

questions.stem: A $12.3\ \text{L}$ vessel at $300\ \text{K}$ contains $4.0\ \text{g}$ of helium and $14.0\ \text{g}$ of nitrogen. Find the total pressure. Take $R=0.082\ \text{L atm mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$, $M(\text{He})=4.0\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$ and $M(\text{N}_2)=28.0\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
The total number of moles is $n=\frac{4.0}{4.0}+\frac{14.0}{28.0}=1.50\ \text{mol}$. Using the ideal gas equation,
$$P=\frac{nRT}{V}=\frac{(1.50)(0.082)(300)}{12.3}=3.0\ \text{atm}.$$

questions.stem: Select the decreasing order of stability of the following anions, considering resonance and cyclic conjugation.

options.text: Cyclopentadienyl anion ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_5^-$) > allyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_5^-$) > propyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_7^-$) > cyclopropenyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_3^-$)
Cyclopentadienyl anion ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_5^-$) > cyclopropenyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_3^-$) > allyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_5^-$) > propyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_7^-$)
Allyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_5^-$) > cyclopentadienyl anion ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_5^-$) > propyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_7^-$) > cyclopropenyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_3^-$)
Cyclopropenyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_3^-$) > cyclopentadienyl anion ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_5^-$) > allyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_5^-$) > propyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_7^-$)

questions.solution: Cyclopentadienyl anion has $6\pi$ electrons and is aromatic; the allyl anion is resonance-stabilized, whereas the propyl anion is localized. The cyclopropenyl anion has $4\pi$ electrons in a cyclic conjugated system and is antiaromatic, so it is least stable. Hence the decreasing order is cyclopentadienyl $>$ allyl $>$ propyl $>$ cyclopropenyl.

questions.stem: Which pairing correctly describes $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ and $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$, respectively?
questions.solution:
Fe$^{2+}$ has configuration $3d^6$. CN$^-$ is a strong-field ligand, so the complex is low-spin and uses inner $d^2sp^3$ hybridisation; all electrons are paired.
H$_2$O is a weak-field ligand, giving a high-spin $sp^3d^2$ complex with four unpaired electrons.
Thus, the pair is $d^2sp^3$, diamagnetic; $sp^3d^2$, paramagnetic.

questions.stem: The ether shown is treated with excess HI. Which pair of organic products forms, and what accounts for the cleavage?

options.text: 2-Iodo-2-methylpropane and iodoethane; cleavage proceeds via the stable tertiary carbocation
1-Iodo-2-methylpropane and iodoethane; cleavage proceeds via a primary carbocation
2-Iodo-2-methylpropane and ethanol; the alcohol is not further cleaved by excess HI
1-Iodopropane and iodomethane; cleavage occurs at both sides of the oxygen

questions.solution:
Protonation of the ether is followed by C–O cleavage at the tertiary side via the stable tert-butyl carbocation:
$$ (CH_3)_3C-O-CH_2CH_3 \xrightarrow{HI} (CH_3)_3C-I + CH_3CH_2OH $$
Excess HI converts ethanol to iodoethane, giving 2-iodo-2-methylpropane and iodoethane.

questions.stem: Taking more negative electron gain enthalpy as higher in the order, which sequence is incorrect?
questions.solution:
More negative electron gain enthalpy ranks higher. Since $\Delta_{eg}H(\text{O})=-141\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta_{eg}H(\text{N})=+7\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$,
$$\text{O} > \text{N}$$
Hence the sequence $\text{N} > \text{O}$ is incorrect.

questions.stem: Given $\Lambda_m^\circ$ values of $\text{HCl}$, $\text{NaCl}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ as $426$, $126$ and $91$ $\text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$, respectively, calculate $\Lambda_m^\circ$ of $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$.
questions.solution:
By Kohlrausch’s law,
$$\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH})=\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{HCl})+\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa})-\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaCl})$$

questions.stem: The energy of the $n=2$ level of hydrogen is $-3.4$ eV. What is the energy of the $n=2$ level of $\text{He}^+$?
questions.solution:
For a hydrogen-like ion, $E_n\propto -\dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}$. At the same $n$, He$^+$ has $Z=2$, so
$$E_2(\text{He}^+)=2^2E_2(\text{H})=4(-3.4)=-13.6\ \text{eV}.$$

questions.stem: Which option gives the shapes of $\text{ClF}_3$, $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{NH}_3$, respectively?

questions.stem: A transition-metal ion has a spin-only magnetic moment of $\sqrt{15}\ \text{BM}$. Which ion can it be?
questions.solution:
The spin-only magnetic moment is $\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}\,\text{BM}$.
$$15=n(n+2)\Rightarrow n=3$$
$\text{V}^{2+}$ has configuration $[\text{Ar}]3d^3$, with three unpaired electrons.

questions.stem: On complete hydrolysis in excess water, which set gives the balanced equations for $\text{PCl}_5$, $\text{SiCl}_4$, and $\text{NCl}_3$, respectively?
questions.solution:
Complete hydrolysis of $\text{PCl}_5$ and $\text{SiCl}_4$ gives phosphoric acid and silica, respectively; $\text{NCl}_3$ hydrolyses to ammonia and hypochlorous acid.
$$\text{PCl}_5+4\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4+5\text{HCl},\quad \text{SiCl}_4+2\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow\text{SiO}_2+4\text{HCl}$$
$$\text{NCl}_3+3\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow\text{NH}_3+3\text{HClO}$$
These equations correspond to (D).

questions.stem: Which statements correctly describe similarities between lithium and magnesium? I. Both form nitrides on direct combination with nitrogen. II. Both carbonates decompose on heating to the oxide and carbon dioxide. III. Both hydroxides are highly soluble in water. IV. Both form superoxides on reaction with oxygen.

$$\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Li}_2\text{O}+\text{CO}_2,\qquad \text{MgCO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{MgO}+\text{CO}_2$$
Mg(OH)₂ is sparingly soluble, and neither metal forms a superoxide; hence only I and II are correct.

questions.stem: What is formed after hydrolysis of the product obtained by reacting $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}$ with $\text{CO}_2$?
questions.solution:
Grignard reagents react with $\text{CO}_2$ to form a carboxylate with one additional carbon atom.
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}+\text{CO}_2\rightarrow\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CO}_2\text{MgBr}\xrightarrow{\text{hydrolysis}}\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$$

questions.stem: Which of the following ions is colourless in aqueous solution?
questions.solution: Scandium(III) has the configuration $\text{Sc}^{3+}:[\text{Ar}]3d^0$. With no $d$ electrons, $d$–$d$ transitions are not possible, so the ion is colourless in aqueous solution.

questions.stem: Among propanal, butanal, 2-methylpropanal and benzaldehyde, which undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction because it has no α-hydrogen? On complete reaction of $0.40$ mol in concentrated aqueous NaOH, followed by acidification, what amounts of alcohol and acid are formed?

options.text: Propanal; $0.20$ mol propan-1-ol and $0.20$ mol propanoic acid
Benzaldehyde; $0.40$ mol benzyl alcohol and $0.40$ mol benzoic acid
Benzaldehyde; $0.20$ mol benzyl alcohol and $0.20$ mol benzoic acid

questions.solution:
Benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction.
$$2\,\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO}+\mathrm{OH^-}\rightarrow\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2OH}+\mathrm{C_6H_5COO^-}$$
Thus, $0.40$ mol benzaldehyde forms $0.20$ mol benzyl alcohol and, after acidification, $0.20$ mol benzoic acid.

questions.stem: For the exothermic equilibrium $\text{N}_2(g)+3\text{H}_2(g)\rightleftharpoons2\text{NH}_3(g)$, which change increases the equilibrium yield of $\text{NH}_3$?

options.text: Increasing the pressure at constant temperature
Increasing the temperature at constant pressure
Adding an inert gas at constant volume

questions.solution:
By Le Chatelier’s principle, increasing pressure shifts the equilibrium toward the side with fewer gaseous moles.
$$4\text{ mol reactants} > 2\text{ mol NH}_3$$
Hence, the equilibrium yield of NH₃ increases.

questions.stem: For the Freundlich isotherm, $\log\dfrac{x}{m}=\log k+\dfrac{1}{n}\log P$. Common-log data give $(\log P,\log(x/m))=(0,-1)$ and $(1,0)$. Which interpretation is correct?

options.text: $n=1$, $k=0.1$, and $\dfrac{x}{m}=0.1P$; the model predicts a finite saturation plateau at high $P$.
$n=1$, $k=10$, and $\dfrac{x}{m}=10P$; the model has no finite saturation plateau and must fail at sufficiently high $P$.
$n=1$, $k=0.1$, and $\dfrac{x}{m}=0.1P$; the model has no finite saturation plateau and must fail at sufficiently high $P$.

questions.solution:
The slope is $1/n$, and the intercept is $\log k$:
$$\frac{1}{n}=\frac{0-(-1)}{1-0}=1,\qquad \log k=-1$$
Hence $n=1$, $k=0.1$, so $\dfrac{x}{m}=0.1P$. The Freundlich isotherm has no finite saturation plateau and must fail at sufficiently high $P$.

questions.stem: An electron and an α-particle are accelerated from rest through the same potential difference. Take $m_\alpha=4m_p$, $m_p=1836m_e$, and their charges as $e$ and $2e$, respectively. Neglect relativistic effects. What is $\lambda_e: \lambda_\alpha$?
questions.solution:
For a particle accelerated through potential difference $V$, $\lambda=h/\sqrt{2mqV}$.
$$\frac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{m_\alpha(2e)}{m_e e}}=\sqrt{8\times1836}=12\sqrt{102}$$
Hence, $\lambda_e: \lambda_\alpha=12\sqrt{102}:1$. (B)

questions.stem: Anions $\text{X}^-$ form a cubic close-packed array. If $\text{M}^{2+}$ ions occupy half the octahedral voids, what is the formula of the solid?
questions.solution:
For $N$ close-packed $\text{X}^-$ ions, the number of octahedral voids is $N$; half occupied gives $N/2$ $\text{M}^{2+}$ ions.
Thus, $n(\text{M}):n(\text{X})=N/2:N=1:2$, so the formula is $\text{MX}_2$.

questions.stem: Arrange the indicated C–O bonds in increasing order of bond length: in $\text{CO}$, $\text{CO}_2$, $\text{HCOO}^-$ and $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$.
questions.solution:
Bond length decreases as bond order increases. The average C–O bond orders are $3$ in CO, $2$ in CO₂, $1.5$ in HCOO⁻ and $4/3$ in CO₃²⁻.
Hence, in increasing order of bond length: $\text{CO} < \text{CO}_2 < \text{HCOO}^- < \text{CO}_3^{2-}$.

questions.stem: The compound shown in the figure is subjected to ozonolysis followed by reductive work-up with Zn/H$_2$O. Which products are formed?

options.text: One molecule each of ethanedial and butane-1,4-dial

questions.solution:
Reductive ozonolysis cleaves both C=C bonds, converting each alkene carbon into a carbonyl group. Cleavage of the ring gives two identical three-carbon fragments:
$$\text{C}_1=\text{C}_2-\text{C}_3-\text{C}_4=\text{C}_5-\text{C}_6-\text{C}_1 \xrightarrow[\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}]{\text{O}_3} 2\,\text{OHC-CH}_2\text{-CHO}$$
Thus, two molecules of propane-1,3-dial are formed.

questions.stem: For the equilibrium $\text{PCl}_5(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3(g)+\text{Cl}_2(g)$, the degree of dissociation is $0.5$ at a total pressure of $2$ atm. Find $K_p$.
questions.solution:
For initial $1$ mol, equilibrium moles are $1-\alpha,\alpha,\alpha$, with total $1+\alpha$.
$$K_p=\frac{p_{\text{PCl}_3}p_{\text{Cl}_2}}{p_{\text{PCl}_5}}=\frac{\alpha^2P}{1-\alpha^2}=\frac{(0.5)^2(2)}{1-(0.5)^2}=\frac{2}{3}\text{ atm}$$

questions.stem: Arrange these compounds in decreasing order of acidity: ethyne, ethene and ethane.
questions.solution:
Greater $s$-character stabilises the conjugate base: $sp > sp^2 > sp^3$.
Thus, the acidity order is ethyne $>$ ethene $>$ ethane, giving (C).

questions.stem: Arrange the following free radicals in decreasing order of stability: benzyl, allyl, tert-butyl and methyl.
questions.solution:
Resonance stabilisation makes benzylic and allylic radicals more stable; benzyl has greater delocalisation. Among alkyl radicals, stability increases with substitution due to hyperconjugation.
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2^\cdot > \text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2^\cdot > (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^\cdot > \text{CH}_3^\cdot$$

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about Group 15 hydrides: I. Thermal stability follows $\text{NH}_3>\text{PH}_3>\text{AsH}_3$. II. Reducing character follows $\text{NH}_3>\text{PH}_3>\text{AsH}_3$. III. Bond angle follows $\text{NH}_3>\text{PH}_3>\text{AsH}_3$. Which statements are correct?
questions.solution: Thermal stability decreases down Group 15, so $\text{NH}_3>\text{PH}_3>\text{AsH}_3$; I is true. Reducing character increases down the group, making II false, while bond angle decreases down the group, so III is true. Hence, I and III only.

questions.stem: Which hydride is ionic and liberates hydrogen gas when it reacts with water?

Hence, $\text{NaH}$ is the required hydride.

questions.stem: On dilution, how do conductivity and molar conductivity change for strong and weak electrolytes?

questions.solution: On dilution, the number of ions per unit volume decreases, so conductivity decreases for both electrolytes. Since $\Lambda_m=\dfrac{\kappa}{c}$, molar conductivity increases slightly for strong electrolytes and sharply for weak electrolytes due to increased ionisation.

questions.stem: An organic compound contains $41.4\%$ carbon, $3.4\%$ hydrogen and $55.2\%$ oxygen. If its molar mass is $58\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$, find its molecular formula. Use atomic masses C = 12, H = 1 and O = 16.
questions.solution:

$$n=\frac{58}{29}=2,\qquad \text{Molecular formula}=(\text{CHO})_2=\text{C}_2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2.$$

questions.stem:
Arrange the four sentences P, Q, R and S between the fixed opening and closing sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

**Opening:** Digital tools can widen access to public knowledge, but access alone does not make a society better informed.

**Middle sentences:**
P. This apparent abundance, however, can obscure the difference between information that is merely available and evidence that has been carefully tested.
Q. The latter requires institutions that explain how claims are checked, corrected and placed in context.
R. Without such institutions, users may mistake repetition for confirmation, especially when a claim is repeated across several platforms.
S. For this reason, expanding access must be accompanied by habits and institutions that help people judge what they encounter.

**Closing:** A well-informed society therefore depends not only on the circulation of knowledge, but also on the means to assess it.

Which is the correct sequence?
questions.solution: P contrasts available information with carefully tested evidence. Q explains what the latter requires, and R shows the risk when those institutions are absent. S then draws the conclusion: access must be paired with ways to judge information.

questions.stem:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

Urban trees are often valued for their appearance, but their contribution to city life is also practical. A tree’s canopy shades pavements and buildings, reducing the amount of heat absorbed during the day. Leaves also release water vapour, which can cool nearby air. Together, these effects may make tree-lined streets more comfortable during hot weather and reduce the need for air-conditioning in some buildings.

Trees can also help manage rainwater. Their leaves and branches intercept some rainfall, while roots and the surrounding soil allow more water to soak into the ground. This can slow the flow of water into drains during heavy showers. However, trees are not a complete solution to urban flooding: soil conditions, drainage design, and the intensity of rainfall also matter.

The benefits of urban trees depend on thoughtful planning. Species must be suited to local conditions, and young trees need care as they become established. Planting decisions should also consider where shade is most needed and whether roots may interfere with pavements or underground services. A city therefore gains more than decoration by maintaining trees, but it cannot rely on planting alone to solve every environmental problem. Trees are most effective when they form part of a wider approach to designing healthy, resilient neighbourhoods.

What is the main idea of the passage?

options.text: Urban trees can eliminate the need for effective drainage systems.
Urban trees provide useful benefits, but require planning and support.
Cities should choose tree species mainly for their visual appearance.
Urban trees are beneficial only during periods of hot weather.

questions.stem: A bag contains $4$ red and $3$ blue balls. If $3$ balls are drawn without replacement, what is the probability of getting exactly $2$ red balls?
questions.solution:
The probability is the number of favourable draws divided by the total number of draws:
$$P=\frac{\binom{4}{2}\binom{3}{1}}{\binom{7}{3}}=\frac{6\cdot3}{35}=\frac{18}{35}.$$

questions.stem: The sum of the first $10$ terms of an AP is $180$. If its $10$th term is three times its first, find $(a,d)$.
questions.solution:
For an AP, $S_{10}=5(2a+9d)=180$, so $2a+9d=36$. The condition $a+9d=3a$ gives $9d=2a$.
$$4a=36\implies a=9,\tag*{}$$
so $d=2$ and $(a,d)=(9,2)$.

questions.stem: Evaluate $\displaystyle \int_0^1 x\left(\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}+\dfrac{1}{1+(1-x)^2}\right)\,dx$.

$$\int_0^1 xg(x)\,dx=\frac12\int_0^1g(x)\,dx=\int_0^1\frac{dx}{1+x^2}=\frac{\pi}{4}.$$

questions.stem: For which values of $a$ and $b$ is $f$ continuous at both $x=1$ and $x=3$? $$f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2+ax,&x<1,\\2ax+b,&1\le x<3,\\x^2+bx,&x\ge3.\end{cases}$$

questions.stem: Evaluate $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{6}k\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{k-1}$.

$$
Thus $S=\frac{9}{16}\div\frac32=\frac38$.

questions.stem: The value of $\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2}+\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}$ is
questions.solution:
Let $A=\tan^{-1}\dfrac12$ and $B=\tan^{-1}\dfrac13$. Then
$$\tan(A+B)=\dfrac{\frac12+\frac13}{1-\frac16}=1.$$
Since $A,B>0$ and $A+B<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, we get $A+B=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$. (B)

questions.stem: An ellipse centered at the origin has vertices $(\pm13,0)$ and $(0,\pm5)$. Its eccentricity is
questions.solution:
For an ellipse, $e=\dfrac{c}{a}$, where $c^2=a^2-b^2$. Here $a=13$ and $b=5$.
$$c=\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=12,\qquad e=\frac{12}{13}$$

questions.stem: Evaluate $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}\dfrac{1-\cos 5x}{x^2}$, where $x$ is in radians.
questions.solution:
Using $1-\cos u\sim \dfrac{u^2}{2}$ as $u\to 0$,
$$\lim_{x\to0}\frac{1-\cos 5x}{x^2}=\lim_{x\to0}\frac{(5x)^2}{2x^2}=\frac{25}{2}.$$

questions.stem: How many odd three-digit numbers can be formed from the digits $0,1,2,3,4$ if no digit is repeated?
questions.solution:
The units digit must be $1$ or $3$: $2$ choices. Then the hundreds digit has $3$ nonzero choices, and the tens digit has $3$ remaining choices.
$$2\times3\times3=18$$

questions.stem: If $|A|=18$, $|B|=15$ and $|A\cup B|=25$, find $|A\cap B|$.
questions.solution:
By the inclusion–exclusion principle,
$$|A\cap B|=|A|+|B|-|A\cup B|=18+15-25=8.$$

questions.stem: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y\tan x=\sin x$, given that $y(0)=1$.
questions.solution:
The integrating factor is $e^{\int \tan x\,dx}=\sec x$, so $\frac{d}{dx}(y\sec x)=\tan x$.
$$y\sec x=-\ln(\cos x)+C$$
Using $y(0)=1$ gives $C=1$, hence $y=\cos x\left(1-\ln(\cos x)\right)$.

questions.stem: Factories A and B supply fractions $p$ and $1-p$ of a product. Their defective rates are $\dfrac1{10}$ and $\dfrac15$, respectively. If the overall defective probability is $\dfrac18$, find the probability a defective item came from A.
questions.solution:
By the law of total probability, $p/10+(1-p)/5=1/8$, giving $p=3/4$.
Using Bayes’ theorem,
$$P(A\mid D)=\frac{pP(D\mid A)}{P(D)}=\frac{(3/4)(1/10)}{1/8}=\frac35.$$

questions.stem: For $f(x)=\dfrac{6x^2-7x-5}{15x^2-46x+35}$ on its natural domain, the range of $f$ is
questions.solution:
Factor and cancel: $f(x)=\dfrac{(3x-5)(2x+1)}{(3x-5)(5x-7)}=\dfrac{2x+1}{5x-7}$, with $x\ne\dfrac{5}{3},\dfrac{7}{5}$.
The value $\dfrac{2}{5}$ is never attained, while excluding $x=\dfrac{5}{3}$ also removes $f\!\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right)=\dfrac{13}{4}$.
Hence the range is $\mathbb{R}\setminus\left\{\dfrac{2}{5},\dfrac{13}{4}\right\}$.

questions.stem: The general solution of $\sin 2x=\sin x$ is
questions.solution:
Using $\sin 2x=2\sin x\cos x$,
$$\sin x(2\cos x-1)=0.$$
Thus $\sin x=0$ gives $x=n\pi$, while $\cos x=\frac12$ gives $x=\pm\frac{\pi}{3}+2n\pi$, where $n\in\mathbb Z$.

questions.stem: The value of $\displaystyle\int x^2\cos x\,dx$ is
questions.solution:
By integration by parts, $\int x^2\cos x\,dx=x^2\sin x-2\int x\sin x\,dx$, and $\int x\sin x\,dx=-x\cos x+\sin x$.
$$\int x^2\cos x\,dx=x^2\sin x+2x\cos x-2\u0000sin x+C$$

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed five times. What is the probability of getting exactly three heads?
questions.solution:
The number of ways to get exactly three heads is $\binom{5}{3}$ out of $2^5$ equally likely outcomes.
$$P(X=3)=\frac{\binom{5}{3}}{2^5}=\frac{10}{32}=\frac{5}{16}$$

questions.stem: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^1\frac{dx}{1+\sqrt{x}}$.
questions.solution:
Let $t=\sqrt{x}$, so $x=t^2$ and $dx=2t\,dt$.
$$\int_0^1\frac{dx}{1+\sqrt{x}}=2\int_0^1\frac{t}{1+t}\,dt=2[t-\ln(1+t)]_0^1=2-2\ln 2$$

questions.stem: The shortest distance between $\mathbf r=\lambda(\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+2\mathbf k)$ and $\mathbf r=6\mathbf k+\mu(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j-2\mathbf k)$ is
questions.solution:
For two skew lines, the shortest distance is $\dfrac{|\mathbf c\cdot(\mathbf b\times\mathbf d)|}{|\mathbf b\times\mathbf d|}$, where $\mathbf b=(1,2,2)$, $\mathbf d=(2,1,-2)$ and $\mathbf c=(0,0,6)$.
$$\mathbf b\times\mathbf d=(-6,6,-3),\qquad \text{distance}=\frac{|18|}{9}=2.$$

questions.stem: The line $y=mx$ touches the circle $(x-2)^2+(y+1)^2=4$. Find $m$.
questions.solution:
The centre is $(2,-1)$ and the radius is $2$. For tangency, the distance from the centre to $y=mx$ must equal the radius:
$$\frac{|2m+1|}{\sqrt{m^2+1}}=2 \implies (2m+1)^2=4(m^2+1) \implies m=\frac{3}{4}.$$

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the $2\times2$ matrix whose entries $(a_{11},a_{12},a_{21},a_{22})$ are $(1,2,2,1)$. Find $A^3-3A^2+I$, giving its entries in row-major order.
questions.solution:
By direct multiplication, $A^2=\begin{pmatrix}5&4\\4&5\end{pmatrix}$ and $A^3=\begin{pmatrix}13&14\\14&13\end{pmatrix}$. Hence
$$A^3-3A^2+I=\begin{pmatrix}-1&2\\2&-1\end{pmatrix},$$
whose row-major entries are $(-1,2,2,-1)$.

questions.stem: The term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left(1+2x^2\right)^5\left(x^3+x^{-1}\right)^4$ is
questions.solution:
Let $i$ count factors of $2x^2$ and $j$ count factors of $x^{-1}$. The general product term has power $x^{2i+12-4j}$, so the constant term requires $2i+12-4j=0$.
Thus $(i,j)=(0,3),(2,4)$, giving
$$\binom{5}{0}\binom{4}{3}+\binom{5}{2}2^2\binom{4}{4}=4+40=44.$$

questions.stem: Find the total area of the two bounded regions enclosed by $y=x^2$ and $y=2|x|$.
questions.solution:
The curves intersect where $x^2=2|x|$, giving $x=-2,0,2$. By symmetry, the total area is
$$A=2\int_0^2(2x-x^2)\,dx=2\left(4-\frac{8}{3}\right)=\frac{8}{3}\text{ square units}.$$

questions.stem: For $f(x)=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)$, where $-1<x<1$, find $f'\!\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)$.
questions.solution:
Using the chain rule and $-1<x<1$,
$$f'(x)=\frac{\frac{2(1-x^2)}{(1+x^2)^2}}{\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)^2}}=\frac{2}{1+x^2}.$$
Hence, $f'\!\left(\frac13\right)=\frac{2}{1+1/9}=\frac95$.

questions.stem: The domain of $f(x)=\sqrt{(x-1)(x-5)}$ is
questions.solution:
For the square root to be defined, $(x-1)(x-5)\geq 0$.
$$x\leq 1\quad\text{or}\quad x\geq 5$$
Hence the domain is $(-\infty,1]\cup[5,\infty)$.

questions.stem: A data set has mean $4$ and variance $3$. If each value $x$ is transformed to $y=-2x+3$, what are the new mean and variance?
questions.solution:
For a linear transformation $y=ax+b$, the mean becomes $a\mu+b$ and the variance becomes $a^2\sigma^2$.
$$\mu_y=-2(4)+3=-5,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(y)=(-2)^2(3)=12$$

questions.stem: A parabola has focus $(3,2)$ and directrix $x=-1$. Its equation is
questions.solution:
The axis is $y=2$, and the vertex midway between the focus and directrix is $(1,2)$. The focal length is $p=3-1=2$.
$$ (y-2)^2=4p(x-1)=8(x-1) $$

questions.stem: For $\vec a=\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$, $\vec b=\hat i+2\hat k$ and $\vec c=2\hat i-2\hat j$, the scalar triple product $[\vec a\,\vec b\,\vec c]$ is
questions.solution:
Using $[\vec a\,\vec b\,\vec c]=\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)$, we get
$$\vec b\times\vec c=4\hat i+4\hat j-2\hat k.$$
Hence $[\vec a\,\vec b\,\vec c]=(1,1,1)\cdot(4,4,-2)=4+4-2=6$.

questions.stem: For complex $z$, if $|z-(1+i)|=2|z-(5+i)|$, the least possible value of $|z|$ is
questions.solution:
Let $z=x+iy$. Squaring the given condition gives
$$(x-1)^2+(y-1)^2=4[(x-5)^2+(y-1)^2],$$
so $(x-\frac{19}{3})^2+(y-1)^2=\frac{64}{9}$. The circle’s centre is $\frac{\sqrt{370}}{3}$ from the origin and its radius is $\frac{8}{3}$; hence the least $|z|=\frac{\sqrt{370}-8}{3}$.

questions.stem: The largest interval on which $f(x)=x^2+2x$ is increasing is
questions.solution:
For an increasing interval, require $f'(x)\geq 0$. Since
$$f'(x)=2x+2\geq 0 \iff x\geq -1,$$
$f$ is increasing on the largest interval $[-1,\infty)$.

questions.stem: The proposition $\sim(p\Rightarrow q)\vee r$ is logically equivalent to
questions.solution:
$p\Rightarrow q\equiv\sim p\vee q$, so by De Morgan’s law, $\sim(p\Rightarrow q)\equiv p\wedge\sim q$.
Hence, $\sim(p\Rightarrow q)\vee r\equiv(p\wedge\sim q)\vee r$.

questions.stem: If $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$ are unit vectors and $\vec a+\vec b+\vec c=\vec 0$, then $\left|\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)+\vec b\times(\vec c\times\vec a)+2\vec c\times(\vec a\times\vec b)\right|$ equals
questions.solution:
Using $\vec x\times(\vec y\times\vec z)=\vec y(\vec x\cdot\vec z)-\vec z(\vec x\cdot\vec y)$, the cyclic sum of the three nested cross products is $\vec 0$. Hence the given vector reduces to $\vec c\times(\vec a\times\vec b)=-\dfrac12(\vec a-\vec b)$, since all pairwise dot products are $-\dfrac12$.
$$\left|\vec c\times(\vec a\times\vec b)\right|=\frac12|\vec a-\vec b|=\frac12\sqrt{2-2\vec a\cdot\vec b}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.$$

questions.stem: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int \frac{\sin x}{2+\cos x}\,dx$.
questions.solution:
Let $u=2+\cos x$, so $du=-\sin x\,dx$. Then
$$\int\frac{\sin x}{2+\cos x}\,dx=-\int\frac{du}{u}=-\ln(2+\cos x)+C.$$

questions.stem: The vowels in the word BALLOON are to occur consecutively. How many such arrangements of its letters are possible?
questions.solution:
Treat the consecutive vowels $AOO$ as one block. The five objects (the block, $B$, $L$, $L$, $N$) can be arranged in $\frac{5!}{2!}$ ways, and the vowels within the block in $\frac{3!}{2!}$ ways.
$$\frac{5!}{2!}\cdot\frac{3!}{2!}=60\cdot3=180$$

questions.stem: Find the distance between the parallel lines $3x+4y-7=0$ and $6x+8y+10=0$.
questions.solution:
For parallel lines $ax+by+c_1=0$ and $ax+by+c_2=0$, $d=\dfrac{|c_2-c_1|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}$. Dividing the second equation by $2$ gives $3x+4y+5=0$.
$$d=\frac{|5-(-7)|}{\sqrt{3^2+4^2}}=\frac{12}{5}$$

questions.stem: For $t\in\mathbb{R}$, the system $$x+ty+(t-1)z=2,\quad x+(2t-1)y+2z=8,\quad (t-1)y+(t-1)z=0$$ has infinitely many solutions and no solution, respectively, for which ordered pair of values of $t$?
questions.solution:
At $t=1$, the third equation becomes $0=0$, while the first two give $z=3$ and $x+y=2$; hence infinitely many solutions.
At $t=2$, the third equation gives $z=-y$, and subtracting the first equation from the second yields $0=6$, so there is no solution.
Thus the ordered pair is $(1,2)$.

questions.stem: The general solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1+\dfrac{y}{x}$ is
questions.solution:
Let $y=vx$. Then $v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=1+v$, so $\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{x}$.
Integrating gives $v=\ln|x|+C$, and hence $y=x(\ln|x|+C)$.
